quest.title: Switcheroo
quest.description: After Sigewinne finally finishes a busy day as head nurse, it seems as though a new problem has already arrived...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x550, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Wait until morning the next day (08:00 – 12:00)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... How is the infirmary even busier than yesterday?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #Good morning, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. I have a few people here for a checkup, so you might need to wait for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problem, anything we can do to help?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Umm... There's a bit of a complicated situation here, I'm still getting to the bottom of it myself...

dialogues.speaker: "Gascon"
dialogues.text: You have to believe me... I'm telling the truth!

dialogues.speaker: Lambersart
dialogues.text: You're in a medical facility. Keep it down!

dialogues.speaker: "Gascon"
dialogues.text: Please, listen to me! I'm not Gascon, I'm Houilles!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: You're a horrible liar, you know that? We get all your mugshots with the arrest warrants. It's clear as day that you're Gascon.

dialogues.speaker: "Gascon"
dialogues.text: You mean because of the way I look? I don't know what happened, I just woke up like this, then you guys dragged me in here for an interrogation...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I brought you here to figure out what's going on. If you truly are the victim of an injustice, yelling isn't going to achieve anything — at most, it'll delay your vindication.

dialogues.speaker: "Gascon"
dialogues.text: ...Alright, I get it.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: This is nuts. Yesterday's interrogations went fine, and now this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Morning, Your Grace. What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Remember the case I mentioned yesterday? The one brought to me by the Marechaussee Phantom? Well, we've been questioning the inmates involved this morning. Every single one of them is claiming mistaken identity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... That's even weirder than what that guy was saying yesterday...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: The thing is, none of them have been able to provide any evidence whatsoever to support their claims. Questioning them further got us nowhere, so for now we've brought them to the infirmary.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And we thought yesterday was as busy as it got for Sigewinne...

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: We've compiled their statements. Have a look. Perhaps there's something we missed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: "Release"? Interesting. The inmates they spoke of in their statements appear to all be due for release today.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: I noticed that too... If that's their plan, they're underestimating us a little. Every serious offender claims they're someone else who just so happens to be due for release today... And they're expecting us to go along with that?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: All the more reason to be cautious. Lambersart, check the release list for today, and make sure no one gets processed. We're gonna need an excuse, though... Just... say we're out of forms. And that we're furiously printing more as we speak.

dialogues.speaker: Lambersart
dialogues.text: I'm on it!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: It's conceivable that our group of serious offenders somehow found a way to switch places with inmates who are about to be released, so they can walk out right under our noses.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: We did consider that possibility, but I mean... Just look at them. They match the warrants, period. How could there have been a switch?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Only if they're dead ringers for the inmates due for release, I suppose... I gave you that name list yesterday to assist in your investigation. Did that help?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Yes, the inmates' mugshots were attached to the list. The first thing I did was check for lookalikes, and I didn't find any.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: The only other thing that stands out to me is that their voices sound a little different today. But it's not exactly hard to put on a fake voice.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Oh, really? Hmm... What does our head nurse make of all this?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Give me a moment. I think I have a way to confirm whether there's been a switch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Isn't that the guy from yesterday?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: This should be Honore. He has very severe facial ulcers, which require an operation in the hospital at the Court of Fontaine. I authorized him to leave the Fortress for medical treatment under guarded escort.

dialogues.speaker: "Potton"
dialogues.text: Yes, like I told you! I'm not Potton! I'm Honore!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: So there has been a swap... Well, I can see what happened in Potton's case, but how do you explain the other inmates? You're not telling me their... souls switched bodies, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: No. I believe it was their faces that got switched.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: The method is a bit like replacing a tooth: Take the bad tooth out, put a false one in. Hmm... And actually, I think I can prove it to you.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, do you remember Erick from the other day?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, sure do!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Then you can be my witnesses. To start with, please fetch the inmate who claims to be Erick.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I know, it's not time to change your dressing yet, but please bear with me.

talks.objective: Find the suspect who claims to be Erick

dialogues.speaker: Lambersart
dialogues.text: Your Grace! Bad news — I paused the releases like you asked, but we were too late... a bunch of people already got processed two hours ago.

dialogues.speaker: Lambersart
dialogues.text: I checked the list, and sure enough... it's all the people who gave statements.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Two hours ago? That's before today's interrogations began... They had this all planned out.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: So there really was a switch after all? Ugh... They really pulled the wool over our eyes on this one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should be able to catch up with them if we leave now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Not if that potion is real. They can just switch faces again after leaving the Fortress. And if the Marechaussee's Melusines can't even spot them, we wouldn't know where to start searching.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes... so we're at a complete dead end!

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: Well... Technically, there is one more lead we could follow up on.

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: We were only able to arrest this gang thanks to the help of a researcher from the Fontaine Research Institute. I believe his name is Rawat.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Oh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Rawat? Isn't that the handsome guy we met at that skincare promotion?

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: Handsome? Maybe from a human point of view. I just remember that he specialized in potions.

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: One of the crimes this gang is charged with is the manufacture and sale of illicit drugs. According Mr. Rawat, they appear to have stolen technology he developed through his research, and used it in their operation.

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: At first, he thought it was a typical case of intellectual property infringement, and he tried to negotiate with them. But once he discovered their criminal operation, he reported them to the authorities.

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: Thanks to his report, we were able to swoop in and arrest them all in one go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a hero. Bet that took courage on his part.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: No doubt. This is worth following up on. As the one who snitched on them, it's highly likely that Rawat will be targeted by the escapees.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: That aside, since he's negotiated with them in person before, there's a chance he'll have some additional information for us.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Understood, Your Grace. My team and I will head to the Fontaine Research Institute right away. In the meantime, please keep an eye on the face-switch victims for us.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Um, Miss Morgane? I'd like to come along and help you catch these criminals.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Well, I'm the one who discharged the fake Erick last night, so I feel partly responsible.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Don't say that, Head Nurse. Your focus was on the inmates' health, and rightly so. We can't ask you to help with arresting criminals — that's our duty.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Umm... I also have a more personal reason. Potton is a patient of mine, and if I don't get a new batch of medicine to him in time, his condition will get much worse.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Look... Head Nurse, I completely understand where you're coming from. But arresting criminals is dangerous business, and if anything happened to you... None of us can afford to take on that responsibility.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I can defend myself just fine.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: You say that, but still—

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: If I may, Ms. Morgane — Sigewinne is the one who raised the potion hypothesis, and I'm sure she has far more expertise on the topic than your team. My suggestion would be to bring her with you.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: And if you really are worried for her safety, then...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon and I are coming along anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Ah, there you go, right on cue. Knew I could count on you.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Okay... Well, since this plan has the Duke's blessing, far be it from me to refuse... We should head off immediately. Time is of the essence.

talks.objective: Go to the Fontaine Research Institute

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Greetings. Sorry to impose, but I'm afraid we're here on urgent business, and we're gonna need you to cooperate.

dialogues.speaker: Bognor
dialogues.text: The Marechaussee Phantom? Let me guess, you're investigating some more illegal research?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Not this time, no. We're looking for a researcher, do you know where we might find Mr. Rawat?

dialogues.speaker: Bognor
dialogues.text: Rawat... Oh, yeah — Mr. Handsome, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just a handful? Paimon figured he'd be the most popular guy around.

dialogues.speaker: Bognor
dialogues.text: Well, I guess you could say he's popular, at least on a superficial level. He's blessed with good looks, so he tends to make a good first impression on people.

dialogues.speaker: Bognor
dialogues.text: But in all his time here at the Fontaine Research Institute, I don't think he's ever had a single deep conversation about his research with his peers. That's no way to make real friends around here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's so weird... He definitely didn't come across like a recluse at that product promotion.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I don't find that weird at all. He definitely didn't strike me as the kind of guy who's good at making friends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Paimon couldn't tell... must be a Melusine perception thing.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Okay — we should talk with his acquaintances, but we also need to check the research institute for any clues. Let's split up, it'll save us some time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure thing. We'll go ask around among the other researchers with Sigewinne. Paimon's suddenly kinda curious to know what everyone really thinks of him.

dialogues.speaker: Bognor
dialogues.text: He actually doesn't work on site here very often. There's a handful researchers in the nearby area who know him pretty well, though. You could see what they know.

talks.objective: Gather intelligence from researchers familiar with Rawat

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there! Are you Antibes?

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: What do you want?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here to ask about Rawat. Any idea where he might be? We were told you're pretty close with him.

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: "Close"? Hmph, not sure that's the word I'd use. He wouldn't even let me use his patent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: It's been a good few days since I last saw him. I don't know where he's at. Go ask someone else.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Umm... Would the patent in question happen to be related to the new skincare product he developed?

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: Tsk... Yeah, kinda. "Butterfly Dew," or whatever he calls it. Hmph, I heard he made a tidy sum off of that one...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, now we're getting somewhere! Keep going...

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: Most of the other researchers here focus on mechanics, energy, stuff like that. I get why he wouldn't be interested in having anything to do with them.

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: But I'm studying coatings. There's a huge overlap in our areas of research! Why would he refuse to work with me?

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: I bought his product once and noticed it contains a unique substance that might have applications in coatings too. If it worked out, I could probably make as much as he's making.

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: Don't get me wrong, I had no intention of plagiarizing his work. I was hoping to get official permission to use his findings in my own research. Followed the proper procedure, it was all above-board — I would've had to pay him a license fee and everything.

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: But despite that, he turned me down not once, not twice, but three times! It's like he's vehemently opposed to the idea of anyone else making the kind of money he does!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so is Rawat antisocial, or is this guy just jealous?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe both of the above...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, doesn't look like we're gonna get any info about Rawat's whereabouts from him. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Wait, one second... Mr. Antibes? Next time you go shopping, you should buy some Bulle Fruits. Peel the skin, steep in water, then drink — it'll help calm your mood.

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: Huh? Uhh, yeah, thanks...

talks.objective: Gather intelligence from researchers familiar with Rawat

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Excuse us, are you Audree?

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: That's me. What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you close friends with Rawat? We're trying to find out where he is.

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: Close friends? Pff. You mean, because I told him I had feelings for him once? I doubt I'm the first or last at the institute to make that mistake... Why would you single me out as a "close friend"?

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: I should've known, really. Men like him, they just enjoy being surrounded by fawning women... They're not interested in a serious relationship.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oookay... Um, we were just kinda wondering if you might know where we can find him...

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: Why would I know where he's at? I barely know him, and he probably doesn't even remember me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, this is getting annoying. Shall we go ask someone else?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Hmm, I think she knows Rawat better than she cares to admit. If we leave now, it might be a wasted opportunity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe, but we're not going to get much out of her while she's in this state, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: She's displaying symptoms common among people in love, if that's what you mean. But I know a cure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...It's curable?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: *clears throat* We're still no closer to finding Mr. Rawat... By this point, he could be in grave danger.

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: Danger? Wait, why are you looking for him, again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh... That's right, yeah! The Marechaussee Phantom said that he's been targeted by some pretty bad people. We need to make sure he's safe.

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: What? How has this happened!? He seemed fine when I last saw him, and that was only a couple of days ago... Just happened to run into him, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I see, I see. Well, do you have any thoughts on where he might be right now?

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: ...Okay, but this is purely out of concern for his safety... If he's not at the Institute, he might be at his mother's place.

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: I heard she raised him alone, that they had it pretty tough financially, and these days she's housebound due to illness. He makes regular trips back home to check on her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, okay. Do you know the address?

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: Nope, sorry. I only found out the thing about his mother because it came up in conversation once. I was just trying to find out more about him. Y'know, so I could get to know him better.

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: When I told him I had a crush on him, I offered to help him take care of his mother. And yeah, maybe that was a stupid idea, but did he really have to yell at me for it? It's like, fine, I can take no for an answer, but what's with the temper tantrum?

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: Unbelievable. Ugh, these guys only wanna show you their charming, well-groomed exterior. They can't stand it when a few home truths shine through...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like her love syndrome is flaring up again...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: We need to find out Mr. Rawat's mother's address... Let's check with the Marechaussee officers when we regroup.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cool, sounds like a plan.

talks.objective: Gather intelligence from researchers familiar with Rawat

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry to bother you, Sir, but are you Bertram?

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: Who's asking?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just some concerned citizens helping out the Marechaussee Phantom with an investigation. We'd like to ask you about Rawat's whereabouts, if that's okay. We're told the two of you are pretty close?

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: Not anymore, we're not. Turns out we don't see eye to eye.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah? What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...The thing about us researchers is, most of us do what we do for some sort of higher purpose. But not Rawat. All he cared about was how to commercialize his findings.

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: He won't even let you work with him unless you sign a confidentiality agreement first. All so he has better control over who gets which intellectual property rights. How are you supposed to get any meaningful research done working with a guy like that?

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: Now that I've got my own technical solution for my compressor, I don't need to work with him anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's what Rawat is really like...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: We'd still like to know where to find him. Is that something you can help us with?

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: Wait, you're... Yeah, I know you, you're the head nurse at the Fortress of Meropide. Alright, then I'm happy to help you if I can. I respect the work you do — medicine serves the highest purpose of all the sciences.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, turns out Sigewinne's got some real clout.

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: Thing is, I have no real way of knowing where he might be. I stopped working with him two months ago, and I've barely seen him since.

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: But if you want my advice, I'd say go talk to the peddlers. There's a few he meets with every other day or so, maybe they know where he's at.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Peddlers?

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: Yeah. Back when I was working with him, I noticed he met with them quite often. Wouldn't surprise me if they were involved in some shady business together, because it seemed like they went out of their way to avoid discussing anything in my presence.

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: The little I overheard was about manufacturing and selling pharmaceutical drugs. Like I said, he's all about the money.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Drugs? Doesn't he work with skincare products? Do those count as drugs?

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: Who knows? I never cared to find out. He's the Mora-grubber, not me.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Thank you. You've given us plenty to work with.

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: Welcome. Goodbye, and may we both reach new heights in our scientific endeavors.

talks.objective: Rendezvous with the Marechaussee Phantom officers

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, Paimon started out thinking Rawat was a handsome researcher with a friendly and cheerful personality. It's such a surprise to learn that his peers have a different impression of him.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: So what's your view of him now, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... A handsome researcher whose difficult upbringing turned him into a profit-chaser with a chip on his shoulder...?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: So your thoughts about his appearance haven't changed at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... His looks are kind of a big deal, at least in Paimon's opinion. How does such a handsome guy end up being so antisocial? Even with his difficult family background, it just doesn't make any sense.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: You can't judge a person solely based on their appearance.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: #Head Nurse, {NICKNAME}, I assume you've spoken with the researchers? What did you find out?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You exchange the intelligence you've gathered.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Bertram mentioned Rawat's involvement with some pharmaceutical merchants. Do you know if he's registered any pharmaceutical brands?

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: Since he was the whistleblower on such a huge case, I ran a background check on him. Hmm... I don't remember there being any brands under his name.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: How strange... If he was so focused on commercializing his research and averse to sharing his technology with others, why wouldn't he have registered his own brands?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Maybe he and his "business partners" needed to avoid public scrutiny?

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: You think he may have colluded with the gang? Hmm... Well, the crime was manufacture and sale of drugs, and that would certainly be in his wheelhouse. We can't rule it out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't that pretty unlikely though? He was the one who blew the whistle on them.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Most children who come to me with tooth decay have suffered pain for a long time already, but they'll still try to hide the fact that they eat too many sweets. Grown-ups and children aren't so different in that regard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, if you say so...

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: I saw him when he came to make his report, and I certainly didn't get the feeling that he was the type to collude with criminals. Perhaps it's more likely that they were coercing him?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: You mentioned that he comes from a poor family. So it's possible that the criminals approached him asking for academic support, luring him in with the promise of riches.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: By the time he discovered who they really were, he was in too deep, they had leverage on him, so he was forced to keep working for them... I've seen it happen many times before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That does make a lot of sense. It would definitely explain why he was so unwilling to cooperate with his fellow researchers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder he's so unsociable. He must be on edge all the time with a gang of crooks breathing down his neck.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: In that case, the situation could be worse than we thought.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: If Rawat was working with the escaped inmates, they're sure to know more about his whereabouts than us. There's a good chance they'll get to him before we do.

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: Based on the information we've gathered so far, he was last seen two days ago. If no one's seen him since, maybe we're... too late...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Two days ago? So he went missing right after that product promotion?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: That was the same day he reported the criminals, too. Not a good sign.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Hmmm... Don't worry, everyone. I believe we still have a chance. Since he disappeared right after blowing the whistle, it's likely that he's gone into hiding.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. He must've been worried that they'd come for him.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: All the more reason to find him as soon as possible. The only lead we have at the moment is his mother's house, which you mentioned earlier. Ceasth, think you can find the place?

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: Yep. *chuckle* When you register a brand, the Court of Fontaine requires you to provide a legal address. The one Rawat wrote down was in the outskirts of the city. That should be the place.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Okay, then there's no time to lose. Let's move!

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: Alright, should be this house. I'm pretty sure this was the address.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Okay, I'll knock.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Morgane knocks several times. No one answers, but you hear the faint sound of breathing from inside.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Sounds like whoever's inside has restricted mobility... It seems serious — what's the fastest way to get this door open?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm... break the door down?

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: No, no, I'll handle it. Let the expert deal with it — there'll be a mountain of paperwork if we damage a citizen's property.

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: Calm down, deep breaths, remember your training, control your strength, aaand... it's open!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: #Ceasth, take a few people and lie in wait. Keep your eyes peeled for any activity around the house. {NICKNAME}, Head Nurse, and I will go inside.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello...! Anyone in here...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There! On the bed, there's an old lady. That's gotta be Rawat's mother, right? She doesn't look like she's in any state to be answering our questions, though...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: We could try, but she is very ill. We mustn't force it.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Well, doesn't look like Rawat's here. She's the only one we can talk to.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Yep... Allow me.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Hello Ma'am, might I ask if you're Rawat's mother? We're trying to locate him.

dialogues.speaker: Sick Old Lady
dialogues.text: Huhhh...? Who...?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Hard of hearing, perhaps... Does anyone have a picture of Rawat?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: I have one here.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I'd like to show you a photo, Ma'am. Is this your son? Do you know where he is?

dialogues.speaker: Sick Old Lady
dialogues.text: *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like this isn't gonna work after all.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...Well, looks like we're out of leads. If Rawat's not here... Things are looking very bad for him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it possible he could have avoided returning here because he knew he'd be in danger?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Maybe, but if so, where do we look next? Maybe we should take another look at the institute?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess so...

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: I suggest we all return there now. We found a good amount of useful information the first time, but perhaps there's something we missed. This is our last hope.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Sorry, Officer, but could I stay here for a while? This patient requires some care.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: #Of course. {NICKNAME}, stay with the head nurse. You're technically here as her assistant, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You got it!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Also, I'd like some Marechaussee members to stay as well and keep an eye on the area.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: If Rawat knows how serious his mother's condition is, he will return.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Got it... Okay, I'll tell the squad members in hiding to stay put and keep a lookout.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #Thanks for helping me out yet again, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problem! But, when you say her condition is serious... Do you mean...?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Yes. She is barely clinging on to life.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Let me take care of a few things first. Could you pass me the towel over there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, of course!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I can tell that her family has tried a lot of different treatment methods, including some very expensive medicines. Unfortunately, her condition is so multifaceted that a recovery looks all but impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sigewinne... Paimon bets being a nurse must be pretty tough at times like this?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Yes... It makes me a little sad.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: In a Melusine's eyes, a human's birth, aging, sickness, and death are as much part of natural law as sunrise and sunset.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: But human medicine can defy that law to some extent. In that sense, it is a science of miracles — that is why I became fascinated with it in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: But it was only after I truly became a doctor that I realized, miracles don't always happen. Even the greatest doctors cannot cure all diseases.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sigewinne...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Don't worry about me, Paimon. A doctor's duty is not to cure all diseases, but to treat whatever ailments they can.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: At the very least, I can lower her fever. That way, she'll suffer less, and she might even be able to see her son.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... All the more reason to find Rawat as soon as possible, even if we don't catch those crooks!

dialogues.speaker: Sick Old Lady
dialogues.text: *cough*...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Her fever's getting worse. Could I get some hot water?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure, we're on the case!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Found it. Fortunately, there's still some ready-made hot water here.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Hmm? This cabinet seems to have a hidden compartment.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is...)

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Found the hot water?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure did! And look what else we found!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Judging by this journal, it seems like Rawat has a private lab. There's a good chance he could be there right now! We gotta go tell Officer Morgane right away!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: That's great news — but hold on just a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: The wet towel is ready. I'm giving you another injection... Are you feeling better now?

dialogues.speaker: Sick Old Lady
dialogues.text: *cough*... Phew...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: It's alright. We'll go bring him back. Please, hang in there.

dialogues.speaker: Sick Old Lady
dialogues.text: ...Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I'll take care of her. Fetch me some hot water, if you would.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The storage trunk has been rifled through, and some essentials are in it. Did Rawat come back previously?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This seems to be a place where a family photo should have been. Why has the photo itself been removed?)

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: So you're... Erick?

dialogues.speaker: "Enri"
dialogues.text: Yes, Head Nurse! It's me! ...You do believe me, right?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I need to do another examination on you. Same procedure as yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: "Enri"
dialogues.text: Alright. It's the cognition test first, right? So I need to concentrate.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Now, try to recall if you can. The last time we did this test, which finger did I hold up?

dialogues.speaker: "Enri"
dialogues.text: I believe it was... your index finger.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But that means...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So basically, last night, the Erick who said he saw another him suddenly recovered and applied to leave the observation ward.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sigewinne did another test before letting him leave, but that time, she held up her pinky finger.

response.speaker: "Enri"
response.text: Huh? Uhh... I don't know about any test last night... There was nothing to do in the observation ward, so I went straight to bed. Then I somehow woke up in a high-security cell.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Hmm. Well, in that case, there is a reasonable explanation for the strange events of the past two days.

response.speaker: Morgane
response.text: So... What exactly happened?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: The gang of serious offenders wanted to break out of prison, so they identified a group of scapegoats — namely, inmates whose terms were almost up — and planned to switch appearances with them.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Last night, when Odilon was on duty, they ambushed him and had one of their group switch appearances with him using their face-swapping method. That allowed them to avoid scrutiny from the other guards.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Then, once all the other inmates were asleep, "Odilon" spent his night shift carrying out the remainder of their switcheroo plan.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: However, they made one mistake. Enri changed his appearance to match Erick's earlier than he should have done, and ended up being spotted by the real Erick.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Real Erick came to the guards for help, but we didn't know then what we know now. So we put it down to hallucination, and sent him to the observation ward.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: However, since one of the gang members was posing as a guard, they simply changed real Erick's appearance and had their "Erick" take his place, muddying the waters even further.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Right... Because I'd put Erick on the observation list by then, and no inmates on that list can be processed for departure until I've discharged them.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Hence why the imposters had to pull that little stunt, to get fake Erick off the list.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... It all makes sense now! The Duke cracked the case!

response.speaker: Morgane
response.text: Well, I can't fault the reasoning. But I'm afraid that we ruled out the possibility of face-switching very early on in this process.

response.speaker: Ceasth
response.text: Criminals altering their facial appearance to commit crimes is nothing new. In fact, one of the explicit duties of the Melusines in the Marechaussee Phantom is to identify criminals in disguise.

response.speaker: Ceasth
response.text: We carefully examined all the suspects, and there is no evidence that any means of disguise were used in this case.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Well then how do we explain all this?

response.speaker: Morgane
response.text: So far, it seems more likely that the gang stole documentation belonging to the inmates due for release, and are using that to commit identity fraud.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Hmm... Actually, there is a potion that can completely change someone's appearance. If they used that... even a Melusine wouldn't be able to detect it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A shape-shifting potion, huh...

response.speaker: Morgane
response.text: Forgive me, Head Nurse, but this is the first time I'm hearing about it... If such a potion truly existed, it would jeopardize our entire investigative process at the Marechaussee Phantom. Are you certain of this?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Yes. I am.

response.speaker: Morgane
response.text: But...

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Please, trust me and my professional opinion as an experienced clinician.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: At the same time, without any solid evidence, it's pure speculation. Hmm... If we can round up all the inmates suspected of switching places, then have a little talk with both sides, we might just get our answer...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Yep, let's do that.

response.speaker: Morgane
response.text: Okay... Well, it was our negligence that meant we had to come and conduct these post-internment interrogations, and I know it's put you out... We'll do it your way.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Looks like our head nurse is relying on you for this one. Thanks in advance.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: What the heck is going on...?

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: How could they switch without me noticing?

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: No, don't look this way. I'm supposed to be hiding, remember? Captain's orders.

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: Gonna have to cut this chat short. I have a patent application to write.

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: Well? I've told you everything I know, don't you think it's time for you to go looking for him? ...Not that I care, obviously...

dialogues.speaker: Bertram
dialogues.text: If my research project works out, the development of underwater spaces should become much easier...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that's all three researchers. Let's head back to the meetup point.
